items.title: Binance hit by record crypto hack estimated at $6.3 billion
items.why: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, says a hack on Thursday night had an estimated impact of about $6.3 billion, of which around $3 billion has been frozen. It says an engineer's laptop was compromised, has paused deposits and withdrawals, and promises to cover all losses.
items.matters: Blockchain firm TRM Labs blames a North Korea-linked group; the previous record theft, from Bybit in 2025, was $1.5 billion.

items.title: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson loses appeal, gets life without parole
items.why: Victoria's Court of Appeal rejected Erin Patterson's appeal against her convictions for murdering three relatives and attempting to murder a fourth with poisonous mushrooms in 2023. It also removed the 33-year minimum term set in 2025, so she will stay in prison for life.
items.matters: AAP says she is only the second woman in Australia given life without parole; she can seek a High Court appeal.

items.title: Atlanta Dream beat Golden State Valkyries to force WNBA Finals Game 7
items.why: The Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 80-69 at home on Thursday to level the WNBA Finals at 3-3. Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard 21; Gabby Williams led Golden State with 26.
items.matters: The deciding Game 7 is in San Francisco on Saturday, 31 October.

items.title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek's Captain Picard, dies at 86
items.why: Sir Patrick Stewart, the British actor who played Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, died at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday, his spokesperson says. He had Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
items.matters: He spent 14 years with the Royal Shakespeare Company before Star Trek made him famous worldwide; he was knighted in 2010.

items.title: Alexander Zverev clinches tennis world No. 1 for the first time
items.why: Germany's Alexander Zverev beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 at the Vienna Open on Thursday, guaranteeing he will top the ATP rankings published on 2 November. He replaces Italy's Jannik Sinner, who ended his season early with a knee injury.
items.matters: He will be the 30th man to reach No. 1, and the first German since Boris Becker in 1991.

items.title: Four Italians killed in EU peacekeeping helicopter crash in Bosnia
items.why: An Italian Chinook helicopter serving with the EU's peacekeeping force in Bosnia and Herzegovina crashed during a training flight near Brčko, in the north, on Thursday. Italy's defence ministry says four Italians died, two soldiers and two Red Cross military volunteers, and 11 people were injured.
items.matters: Italy's defence minister says none of the injured are in critical condition; the EU force, EUFOR, is investigating the cause.

items.title: Flash floods kill at least five in northern and eastern Syria
items.why: Heavy rain since Wednesday has caused flash floods across northern and eastern Syria. Syria's emergencies ministry says at least five people died, four of them children who drowned in Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor provinces, and five more are missing. A bridge collapse has cut the Raqqa–Aleppo road.
items.matters: Rescuers have evacuated at least 375 families from three displacement camps in Raqqa province, state media report.

items.title: Finnish police open criminal inquiry into forest clearing for Google data centre
items.why: Police in Oulu, northern Finland, are investigating suspected environmental damage at a Google data centre site in Muhos, where Google's Finnish subsidiary cleared about 330 hectares of forest before required environmental assessments were done. Regulators had already halted work there and at a second site in Kajaani.
items.matters: Google apologised and says it believed it acted lawfully; police expect the inquiry to run into 2027.

items.title: Christine Lagarde to leave the European Central Bank early, in February
items.why: The ECB says its president, Christine Lagarde, will step down on 7 February 2027, about nine months before her term ends; no reason was given. Later on Thursday the bank held its deposit rate at 2.5%, with eurozone inflation at 3.8%, Euronews reports.
items.matters: Eurozone leaders must now choose who will steer interest rates for 21 countries while inflation is well above target.

items.title: South Africa picks Durban for its 2036 or 2040 Olympic bid
items.why: South Africa's Olympic committee named Durban, on the east coast, as its main candidate city for the 2036 or 2040 Summer Games on Thursday, with cabinet backing. Rivals include Munich, Ahmedabad, Istanbul, Budapest, Qatar and South Korea's Jeonbuk region.
items.matters: Africa has never hosted the Olympics; the IOC plans to choose the 2036 host in 2029.

items.title: Pompeii cupboard sealed by Vesuvius reveals cosmetics, coins and a charm necklace
items.why: Archaeologists at Pompeii, near Naples in Italy, have recovered the contents of a cupboard buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79: make-up tools, an incense burner, a bronze lamp, 38 bronze coins in a woven basket and a necklace of tiny amulets.
items.matters: Such charm necklaces were usually given to children; the park's director says the owner's identity cannot be known for certain.

items.title: Russian drone strike on Dnipro railway station kills at least 14
items.why: A Russian drone hit a platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, central Ukraine, at about 11am on Thursday as a train prepared to leave. Regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha says at least 14 people were killed and 14 injured, six of them seriously.
items.matters: President Zelensky called the attack horrific and urged allies not to ease sanctions on Russia.
items.changed: Updated: the death toll rose to 14, the regional governor says

items.title: Hong Kong's leader apologises as fire inquiry blames weak oversight
items.why: An independent inquiry into last November's Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people, says it was most likely started by a cigarette and found failings at four government bodies. Chief Executive John Lee apologised, and Housing Secretary Winnie Ho has resigned.
items.matters: Officials at four agencies now face a three-month review for possible neglect of duty.

items.title: Hello Kitty maker Sanrio drops Japanese spy drama tie-in after Chinese backlash
items.why: Sanrio's Chinese arm has cancelled merchandise showing Hello Kitty and other characters dressed as spies from the TBS drama Vivant, and apologised. Chinese state media had criticised the show, which depicts Chinese agents torturing Japanese spies. TBS says the series is fiction.
items.matters: It shows how strained China–Japan relations are spilling over into entertainment and brands.

items.title: UN says Afghanistan's opium harvest grew fivefold despite the Taliban ban
items.why: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime says land under opium poppy in Afghanistan rose by 330% this year to over 43,000 hectares, and estimated output rose from about 300 to almost 1,500 tonnes. Taliban authorities say they destroyed 22,000 hectares.
items.matters: It is still far below the 232,000 hectares grown before the 2022 ban; the UN says farmers lack alternatives.

items.title: North Korea fires about ten ballistic missiles towards the sea
items.why: North Korea fired around ten short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan, on its east coast, at about 12:30 local time on Thursday, South Korea's military says. They flew about 250 km into the sea; Japan says they landed outside its exclusive economic zone.
items.matters: It comes a week after Seoul offered military talks over a border landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

items.title: Brewers beat Rays to win their first World Series
items.why: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 in St. Petersburg, Florida, on Wednesday night to win the best-of-seven series 4-1. Rookie Cooper Pratt drove in two runs, and Jacob Misiorowski pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings.
items.changed: Updated: Milwaukee won Game 5 and the series 4-1
items.matters: It is the Brewers' first title since the club began in 1969.

items.title: Samsung's quarterly profit tops 100 trillion won for the first time
items.why: Samsung Electronics made an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (about $80 billion) in July to September, up more than 780% on a year earlier, driven by demand for AI memory chips. It will pay a 30 trillion won dividend. Its shares fell more than 5% on Thursday morning.
items.matters: The chip division missed some investors' expectations, Bloomberg reports, showing how high hopes for AI profits have become.

items.title: Alphabet shares fall about 10% after profit and advertising miss forecasts
items.why: Google's parent Alphabet made a net profit of $26.2 billion in July–September, down 25% on a year earlier and below forecasts, partly due to an $8.7 billion loss linked to its SpaceX stake. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion; cloud revenue more than doubled.
items.matters: Investors are questioning whether AI spending, forecast at up to $205 billion this year, will pay off.

items.title: US Federal Reserve holds rates as two officials push for a rise
items.why: The Fed kept its main rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, by a vote of 10 to 2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted another rise. US inflation reached 3.7% in September, driven mainly by energy prices.
items.matters: Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is too high; traders now expect a rise in December.

items.title: US farmworkers' leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
items.why: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez in the 1960s, died of cancer on Wednesday, her family says. She coined the slogan 'Sí, se puede' ('Yes, we can') and campaigned for decades for farmworkers, women and civil rights.
items.matters: Her slogan was later taken up by Barack Obama's 2008 campaign; he awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.

items.title: Anorexia and bulimia cases have risen 71% worldwide since 1990
items.why: About 18.1 million people had anorexia or bulimia in 2023, a Global Burden of Disease study in JAMA Psychiatry estimates. Much of the rise reflects population growth; rates rose about 21%. Australia had the highest rate and the fastest increases were in East, South and South-East Asia.
items.matters: Around 41% of cases are in people aged 10 to 24, and the researchers forecast nearly 22 million cases by 2050.

items.title: EU drops 'associate member' label for Canada ahead of Montreal summit
items.why: The EU has removed the idea of Canada becoming an 'associate member' from the draft statement for its two-day summit with Canada in Montreal, which starts on Thursday. Diplomats say Germany led objections because the term has no legal status; the text now says 'ever closer association'.
items.matters: Both sides want closer trade and defence ties as they face US tariffs; formal talks are expected to take another year.

items.title: Bank of Canada raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
items.why: Canada's central bank raised its key rate by a quarter point to 2.5% on Wednesday, its first rise since July 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said it was needed so that high energy prices do not spread through the economy. Inflation was 3.2% in September, Al Jazeera reports.
items.matters: Higher rates mean dearer mortgages and loans; the bank says it may need to raise them again.

items.title: European gas price passes €100 for the first time since 2022
items.why: Europe's benchmark Dutch TTF gas price briefly reached €100 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, the first time since December 2022 and about three times its level before the Iran war. EU storage is about 75% full, below the usual target for early November.
items.matters: Most of the rise is expected to reach household bills in 2027; the EU's energy commissioner warned of 'another energy crisis'.

items.title: Up to 50,000 people flee clashes in southern Ethiopia into Kenya
items.why: Fighting between the regional forces of Ethiopia's Somali and Oromia regions around the border town of Moyale began on 20 October. The UN refugee agency says up to 50,000 people have crossed into Kenya, citing local authorities. Several people have died, sources told AFP.
items.matters: Many are sheltering in schools and churches in Kenya's Moyale County; UNHCR says numbers are still rising.

items.title: Putin hosts African leaders at Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
items.why: Delegations from 48 African countries, 22 led by their heads of state, are at the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow this week. President Vladimir Putin said Russia does not practise 'neo-colonial exploitation' and offered grain, fertiliser and help with infrastructure. He accused Western countries of trapping African nations in debt.
items.matters: Russia is competing with Western countries and China for trade and influence in Africa; a final declaration is expected.

items.title: At least 69 killed as two high-speed trains collide in central Spain
items.why: A Renfe high-speed train hit a stationary Iryo train near Urda, in Toledo province, on Wednesday morning, killing at least 69 people, Spain's transport ministry says. Transport Minister Óscar Puente says a control centre wrongly let the Renfe train resume after a signalling fault.
items.matters: A court in Toledo province has taken over the investigation and ordered the trains' black boxes to be seized, Euronews reports.
items.changed: Updated: the death toll rose to 69, Spain's transport ministry says
Updated: Iran now says four tankers were hit; a UK agency reports two incidents
items.title: Iran says four tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers caught fire after hitting mines on a Hormuz route Iran has not authorised; Iran's military says a fourth was hit further east. Britain's UKMTO agency reports one ship on fire and another tanker attacked, without giving a cause.
items.matters: The US says the main shipping lanes are clear of mines; none of Iran's claims has been independently confirmed.

items.changed: Updated: he has landed in Miami and says he is Brazil's rightful leader
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after leaving Brazil despite court order
items.why: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate landed in Miami on Wednesday with his family, after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador despite a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports in a money-laundering inquiry, which he denies. The US granted the family visas. In a letter, he called himself Brazil's rightful leader.
items.matters: Brazil's electoral court, international observers and his own party have recognised President Lula's re-election.

items.changed: Updated: the count is complete and the deadlock holds
items.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock, with neither bloc reaching a majority
items.why: With the count complete, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, official results show; 61 are needed. Arab-led parties won 19 seats. Netanyahu's Likud is the largest single party, with 27.
items.matters: The elections committee is due to certify the results by 4 November; coalition talks could take weeks, and another election is possible.

items.title: Aid convoy heads for Russian-held Oleshky as local ceasefire holds
items.why: Ukraine's and Russia's human rights commissioners say routes into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, have been cleared of mines. An aid convoy set off overnight, Russian media report, and residents who want to leave can do so until 2pm local time on Friday.
items.matters: Fewer than 2,000 people remain in a town of 24,000 before the war; the ceasefire is due to last until 1 November.
items.changed: Updated: mines are cleared and an aid convoy is on its way
